claims.text: Rapid, high-energy heating can make the noble-metal precursors reduce sufficiently quickly and nearly simultaneously.
Nearly simultaneous precursor reduction causes nearly concurrent nanoparticle nucleation.
Nearly concurrent nucleation promotes homogeneous high-entropy alloy nanoparticle formation.
The proposed starting material is a mixture of noble-metal salts or complexes dispersed on a high-surface-area support.
A steep temperature ramp produces a burst of supersaturation in metal atoms.
The supersaturation burst induces abundant, nearly simultaneous nucleation events.
Nearly simultaneous nucleation overcomes differences in the individual precursors' reduction kinetics.
Nearly simultaneous nucleation suppresses sequential growth that would otherwise lead to phase segregation.
Synchronous reduction limits the formation of large compositionally segregated domains.
Synchronous reduction promotes interdiffusion at nucleation sites and thereby yields a homogeneous alloy.
Slower heating permits selective reduction and sequential nucleation.
Selective reduction and sequential nucleation lead to phase separation or elemental segregation.
Relative to slow heating, rapid heating should produce nanoparticles with a more uniform elemental distribution.
Relative to slow heating, rapid heating should produce a more nearly single-phase alloy structure.
Narrower diffraction peaks are expected to indicate the proposed single-phase alloy structure.
The slow-heating baseline is expected to exhibit substantial elemental segregation and phase heterogeneity.
The mechanism should apply when precursor chemical properties and reduction potentials are sufficiently similar for heating kinetics to control reduction synchrony.
The mechanism may fail when disparities among precursor reduction kinetics are too large to overcome.
The mechanism may not apply to non-noble-metal systems because their structural or chemical dynamics may differ.
Precursor solubility and support interactions may influence whether synchronous reduction occurs.
